info.title: Gatekeep Admin API
info.description: The Admin Dashboard's API on Host.Admin: the Deployment surface under /api/v1/deployment and the Tenant surface under /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}, whose Tenant comes from that path segment only. Every endpoint but the bootstrap claim and Admin sign-in needs the __Host-gk-admin Session cookie; every state-changing one also needs the exact Admin Origin and the Session's X-Gatekeep-CSRF token. The claim and sign-in need the exact Admin Origin only. Each operation's x-gatekeep-access names its one access declaration: a capability from the capability table, self-service, or sessionless. A refusal's body is only a fixed code and the trace ID.

post.summary: Claim bootstrap with the one-time token and create the first Admin.
post.description: Consumes the token from gatekeep init, creates the first Admin as Deployment Owner, completes bootstrap and starts a setup-restricted Admin Session in one transaction. Needs the exact Admin Origin, and has no session or CSRF check. Each claim is counted per client before the token is compared: the sixth in 15 minutes is 429. Once bootstrap is complete, or before init, it is the unknown-path 404.

Set-Cookie.description: The Admin Session: __Host-gk-admin={43 base64url characters}; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict. A browser session cookie, with no Domain, Expires or Max-Age.

403.description: Forbidden

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until this client's claim window ends and it may claim again.

post.summary: Begin an Admin sign-in with WebAuthn: the options for navigator.credentials.get.
post.description: Sessionless: needs the exact Admin Origin, and has no session or CSRF check. Returns request options for the Admin RP ID with user verification required and no allowed credentials listed: the credential is discoverable, so no username is asked for and no credential ID is sent. Sets the __Host-gk-admin-signin cookie that binds the challenge to this browser; it can be answered once, within 5 minutes, and a new begin replaces it. Each begin is counted per client: the 21st in 15 minutes is 429. Before bootstrap completes it is the unknown-path 404.

Set-Cookie.description: The sign-in binding: __Host-gk-admin-signin={43 base64url characters}; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=300. The complete call must carry it.

403.description: Forbidden

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the rate-limit window allows another request.

post.summary: Complete an Admin sign-in with the browser's WebAuthn assertion, and start a full Admin Session.
post.description: Sessionless: needs the exact Admin Origin and the __Host-gk-admin-signin cookie from the begin. Once the call is counted, the challenge that cookie names is taken before the body is read, so it is used up whatever follows, and every response clears the cookie. A 429, or a 503 for a missing client address, comes before that and leaves the challenge live. Verifies the assertion against the Admin RP ID, the exact Admin origin and the registered credential it names, with user verification, the credential owner's user handle and a signature counter that advances. Every refusal is the same 400 signin_refused, with no Session. A sign-in starts a full Session; an Admin without two credentials still reaches only setup. A live Session this browser held is ended as superseded. Each complete is counted per client, a success too: the 11th in 15 minutes is 429. Before bootstrap completes it is the unknown-path 404.

Set-Cookie.description: The Admin Session: __Host-gk-admin={43 base64url characters}; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict, a browser session cookie with no Domain, Expires or Max-Age. And __Host-gk-admin-signin cleared with Max-Age=0, as on every complete.

403.description: Forbidden

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the rate-limit window allows another request.

get.summary: The current Admin Session and its CSRF token.
get.description: Setup-allowed and recovery-allowed, and read-only: the CSRF token is the Session's, the same each time and in every tab. recoveryCodeAllowed says whether credential setup may offer an offline Recovery Code.

delete.summary: Sign out: end the current Admin Session.
delete.description: Ends the Session as signed_out, writes admin.session.signed_out, and clears the cookie. Setup-allowed and recovery-allowed: any Session can always sign out. A Deployment Owner who signs out of setup before registering a credential can't sign in again without gatekeep recover-admin.

403.description: Forbidden

post.summary: Begin registering a WebAuthn credential: the options for navigator.credentials.create.
post.description: Setup-allowed. Returns creation options for the Admin RP ID and origin, with no attestation, user verification required, a resident key required, ES256 and RS256, and the Admin's credentials excluded. Its challenge can be answered for 5 minutes, by the next complete call only; a new begin replaces it. In a setup or recovery Session it needs nothing more: a setup Session registers while its Admin is below the floor of two credentials, or one and a Recovery Code, and is refused with a bodiless 403 after; a recovery Session registers once. In a full Session it adds a credential: it is 409 credentials_maximum at 10, before anything else, then needs a fresh assertion for self.credentials.add, which it uses up, or is 403 fresh_assertion_required. Each begin and complete counts towards 10 per Session in 15 minutes, then 429.

403.description: fresh_assertion_required, with the problem body, when no fresh assertion for this action and target is bound to the Session. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a restricted Session, or a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the rate-limit window allows another request.

post.summary: Complete a WebAuthn credential registration with the browser's attestation response.
post.description: Setup-allowed. Verifies the response against the pending challenge, the Admin RP ID and the exact Admin origin, and stores the credential. The challenge is used up whatever the outcome. A response for another RP ID or origin, a cross-origin one, one without user verification, one with no live challenge and one returning an existing credential are 400 credential_refused, with nothing stored. The challenge is taken before the body is read. A credential that brings the Admin to the floor completes setup, and one registered in a recovery Session ends it: the Session becomes full. Refused with a bodiless 403 when a restricted Session's Admin already meets the floor, and 409 credentials_maximum at 10.

403.description: Forbidden

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the rate-limit window allows another request.

get.summary: The Deployment capabilities the current Admin holds.
get.description: Self-service: any Admin may read their own list. Every Deployment capability for the Deployment Owner, in the table's order, and none for any other Admin: a Tenant Role grants no Deployment capability. Not setup-allowed: a setup Session gets 403.

403.description: Forbidden

get.summary: The Tenant capabilities the current Admin holds in the path Tenant.
get.description: The Tenant is the tenantId path segment, its public ID, and nothing else: no Session, cookie or header names one. Returns the capabilities the Admin's Tenant Role there holds, in the table's order. Being Deployment Owner adds nothing in a Tenant. A malformed, unknown or role-less Tenant is the same 403 access_denied, and writes admin.access.denied while the Admin is within 30 audited refusals in 15 minutes, and is only logged past that. A setup-restricted Session, a wrong Origin or a wrong CSRF token gets a bodiless 403 first. The role is read once per request, by the check that allows it, and the list is answered from that same read.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The Tenant's public ID: ten_ and the UUID's 16 bytes in lowercase RFC 4648 base32 with no padding, whose last character carries two zero bits. Only this canonical spelling, after URL decoding, names a Tenant, and the empty UUID's never does; anything else is refused like a Tenant the Admin holds no role in.

403.description: access_denied, with the problem body, when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a Session restricted to setup, or on a state-changing call a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

post.summary: Begin confirming a sensitive action with a fresh WebAuthn assertion: the options for navigator.credentials.get.
post.description: Self-service, full Sessions only. The body names the action, a Deployment capability whose fresh assertion isn't never or self.credentials.add or self.credentials.remove, and its target exactly as the action's request will name it, or null. An unknown action, a Tenant capability or a body that isn't JSON is 400 assertion_refused; a Deployment capability the Admin doesn't hold is 403 access_denied, counted and audited as the request checks do. Returns request options for the Admin RP ID with user verification required and no credential listed. The challenge can be answered once, within 5 minutes, and a new begin replaces it and any unused grant for the same action and target. Each begin and complete counts towards 10 per Session in 15 minutes, then 429.

403.description: Forbidden

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the rate-limit window allows another request.

post.summary: Complete a fresh WebAuthn assertion, leaving a grant on the Session for the begin's action and target.
post.description: Self-service, full Sessions only. Once counted, the Session's pending challenge is taken before the body is read, so it is used up whatever follows. Verifies the assertion as sign-in does, against one of the Session's own Admin's credentials, with user verification, their user handle and a signature counter that advances. A pass stores a grant bound to this Session and the begin's action and target for 5 minutes, writes admin.fresh_assertion.verified and is 204. The grant is used up by the first request it matches, whatever that request then does. Every refusal is the same 400 assertion_refused, with no grant.

403.description: Forbidden

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the rate-limit window allows another request.

get.summary: Your credentials: the current Admin's own WebAuthn credentials, oldest first.
get.description: Self-service, full Sessions only. Each credential's acr_ public ID, kind, backup state, when it was added and last used, and whether removing it would keep the floor of two; and whether the Admin holds a confirmed, unused Recovery Code. Never a WebAuthn credential ID, public key, AAGUID, counter or user handle.

403.description: Forbidden

delete.summary: Remove one of the current Admin's own WebAuthn credentials.
delete.description: Self-service, full Sessions only, after a fresh assertion for self.credentials.remove with this credentialId as its target, which the request checks use up before anything else, or 403 fresh_assertion_required. A malformed, unknown or another Admin's credential is 404. A removal that would leave fewer than two credentials is 409 credentials_minimum. Otherwise it deletes the credential, ends every other live Session of the Admin as revoked, writes admin.credential.removed and is 204; this Session stays. When the credential removed is the one whose fresh assertion confirmed it, this Session ends too: 200 with sessionEnded true, and the cookie cleared.

403.description: fresh_assertion_required, with the problem body, when no fresh assertion for this action and target is bound to the Session. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a restricted Session, or a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

post.summary: Issue an offline Recovery Code in place of a second credential, shown this once.
post.description: Setup-allowed, and only in a setup Session of an Admin who isn't the Deployment Owner, with exactly one credential and no confirmed code; otherwise a bodiless 403. Returns the code once, never cached; only its HMAC under the Deployment hmac key is stored, unconfirmed, replacing any unconfirmed one. It can't be redeemed until confirmed. A key custody failure is 503 with nothing stored.

403.description: Forbidden

post.summary: Confirm the offline Recovery Code was saved, which completes credential setup.
post.description: Setup-allowed, under the same rule as the issue; otherwise a bodiless 403. The body names the issueId the issue returned: when it isn't the Admin's current unconfirmed code, as after a later issue, it is 409 recovery_code_superseded and nothing changes. Confirms the code, writes admin.recovery_code.issued, makes the Admin's setup Sessions full, writes admin.setup.completed and is 204.

403.description: Forbidden

post.summary: Sign in with an offline Recovery Code, to a Session that reaches only credential registration.
post.description: Sessionless: needs the exact Admin Origin only. Each call is counted Deployment-wide, then per client, before the code is read: the 51st across the Deployment, or a client's 6th, in 15 minutes is 429. A confirmed, unused code is used up, every live Session of its Admin ends as revoked, a live Session this browser held is superseded, and a recovery Session starts, which reaches only the Session read, sign-out and credential registration until one credential is registered, which ends every other Session of the Admin; admin.recovery_code.used is written. A wrong, unconfirmed, used or malformed code is the same 400 recovery_code_refused. A key custody failure is 503 with nothing used. Before bootstrap completes it is the unknown-path 404.

Set-Cookie.description: The recovery Admin Session: __Host-gk-admin={43 base64url characters}; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict, a browser session cookie with no Domain, Expires or Max-Age.

403.description: Forbidden

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the rate-limit window allows another request.

post.summary: Sign in with a gatekeep recover-admin enrolment, to a Session that reaches only credential registration.
post.description: Sessionless: needs the exact Admin Origin only. No route issues an enrolment: only gatekeep recover-admin on the Docker host does, after its Security Alert and off-server record are confirmed. Each call is counted per client, then, while the client is within its limit, Deployment-wide, before the value is looked up: a client's 6th, or the 51st counted across the Deployment, in 15 minutes is 429. An unused enrolment within its 15 minutes is used up, with every other unused one of its Admin, every live Session of its Admin ends as revoked, a live Session this browser held is superseded, and a Session starts that reaches only the Session read, sign-out and credential registration: setup, needing two credentials, for an Admin below the credential floor, and recovery, needing one, otherwise; admin.enrolment.used is written. An unknown, used, expired or malformed value is the same 400 enrolment_refused. Before bootstrap completes it is the unknown-path 404.

Set-Cookie.description: The setup or recovery Admin Session: __Host-gk-admin={43 base64url characters}; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict, a browser session cookie with no Domain, Expires or Max-Age.

403.description: Forbidden

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the rate-limit window allows another request.

get.summary: The Deployment's Tenants, oldest first, 50 a page, and the Tenant zone their hosts sit under.
get.description: Deployment Owner only. Each Tenant's ten_ public ID, name, host as stored at creation, label, status and creation time; while it is creating, its creation Operation's opr_ ID and whether it is running or failed; while it is deleting, its deletion Operation's, alike. A deleted Tenant is never listed. No subdomain is split out of a host. nextCursor is the last Tenant's ID when another page follows, else null; pass it back as cursor, which works even when it names a Tenant deleted since. A malformed cursor is 400 tenant_invalid.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The previous page's nextCursor: a ten_ public ID. Anything else is 400 tenant_invalid.

403.description: access_denied, with the problem body, when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a Session restricted to setup, or on a state-changing call a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

post.summary: Create a Tenant with its permanent Tenant Subdomain, and start the Operation that finishes it.
post.description: Deployment Owner only. The only request that takes a Tenant Subdomain: it can never be changed, and a host once issued is never reused. In one transaction it stores the Tenant as creating, with its host and the issuer, WebAuthn RP ID and email link base derived from it once; makes the caller its Tenant Owner; starts its tenancy.tenant.create Operation; and writes tenancy.tenant.created. The Operation creates the Tenant's keys, then its settings, and makes it active; until then its host isn't served. A body that isn't JSON, is over 4096 bytes, misses a field or has the wrong type, and an invalid name or label, is 400 tenant_invalid. A malformed, reserved or taken subdomain is the same 400 subdomain_refused, which never says which. Location names the Operation on the Tenant's own path.

403.description: access_denied, with the problem body, when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a Session restricted to setup, or on a state-changing call a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

post.summary: Retry a failed Tenant creation's failed steps.
post.description: Deployment Owner only. Reopens only the failed steps of a failed tenancy.tenant.create Operation, which runs again, and writes operations.operation.retried. One that is running or succeeded is 409 operation_not_failed, and one whose Tenant is being deleted, or deleted, is 409 tenant_deleted, and never runs again. An Operation of any other type, a deletion included, and an unknown or malformed operationId, is the unknown-path 404.

403.description: access_denied, with the problem body, when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a Session restricted to setup, or on a state-changing call a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

post.summary: Delete a Tenant: its host stops resolving, every Tenant Role in it ends, and its deletion Operation starts.
post.description: Deployment Owner only, after a fresh assertion for deployment.tenants.delete with this targetTenantId as its target, begun on POST /api/v1/deployment/assertions, which the request checks use up before anything else, whatever follows, or 403 fresh_assertion_required: a refusal after it needs a new confirmation. The body's confirmation must be the Tenant's host exactly as the Tenants list shows it, with no trimming or case folding, or 400 confirmation_mismatch. In one transaction it sets the Tenant deleting, so its host gets the same 404 as an unknown host at once; removes every Tenant Role in it, so every Tenant route refuses its former members; starts its tenancy.tenant.delete Operation; and writes tenancy.tenant.deletion_started. The Operation purges every module's data of the Tenant but its Logs, destroys its keys and marks it deleted; its Logs are kept for at least 90 days after, whatever its label. The Tenant and its host are never reused. A body that isn't JSON, is over 4096 bytes, or misses confirmation or has the wrong type is 400 tenant_invalid. A Tenant already being deleted, or deleted, is 409 tenant_deleted, and one whose creation is still running 409 tenant_busy. An unknown or malformed targetTenantId is the unknown-path 404. Location names the deletion.

403.description: fresh_assertion_required, with the problem body, when no fresh assertion for this action and target is bound to the Session; access_denied when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a restricted Session, or a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

get.summary: A Tenant's newest deletion Operation, with every step.
get.description: Deployment Owner only. The newest tenancy.tenant.delete Operation of the Tenant, whatever its status, with every step's codes and IDs, never a step's row ID. A Tenant never deleted, and an unknown or malformed targetTenantId, is the unknown-path 404.

403.description: access_denied, with the problem body, when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a Session restricted to setup, or on a state-changing call a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

post.summary: Retry a Tenant's failed deletion's failed steps.
post.description: Deployment Owner only, after a new fresh assertion for deployment.tenants.delete with this targetTenantId as its target, which the request checks use up, or 403 fresh_assertion_required. No body and no typed confirmation. Reopens only the failed steps of the Tenant's failed tenancy.tenant.delete Operation, which runs again, and writes operations.operation.retried. A deletion that is running or succeeded, and a Tenant that isn't being deleted, is 409 operation_not_failed. An unknown or malformed targetTenantId is the unknown-path 404.

403.description: fresh_assertion_required, with the problem body, when no fresh assertion for this action and target is bound to the Session; access_denied when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a restricted Session, or a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

get.summary: One Operation as the path Tenant sees it: only its own steps.
get.description: Any Tenant Role in the path Tenant. Codes and IDs only, never a step's row ID. Another Tenant's Operation, an unknown one and a malformed operationId are the same unknown-path 404. A malformed, unknown or role-less Tenant is 403 access_denied, audited as every Tenant capability refusal is.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The Tenant's public ID: ten_ and the UUID's 16 bytes in lowercase RFC 4648 base32 with no padding, whose last character carries two zero bits. Only this canonical spelling, after URL decoding, names a Tenant, and the empty UUID's never does; anything else is refused like a Tenant the Admin holds no role in.

403.description: access_denied, with the problem body, when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a Session restricted to setup, or on a state-changing call a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

get.summary: The active Tenants the current Admin holds a Tenant Role in, for the Tenant switcher.
get.description: Self-service, full Sessions only: any Admin may read their own list. Each active Tenant the Admin holds a Tenant Role in, oldest first, with its ten_ public ID, name, host as stored at creation and label; never the role, and no Tenant still being created. A Deployment Owner holding no Tenant Role gets an empty list, as any other Admin does. No paging. A setup or recovery Session gets 403.

403.description: Forbidden

get.summary: The path Tenant's environment label: dev, staging or prod.
get.description: Any Tenant Role in the path Tenant, whatever the Tenant's status, which it returns too: only an active Tenant's label changes. It takes no lock, so it never waits behind a change. A malformed, unknown or role-less Tenant is 403 access_denied, audited as every Tenant capability refusal is.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The Tenant's public ID: ten_ and the UUID's 16 bytes in lowercase RFC 4648 base32 with no padding, whose last character carries two zero bits. Only this canonical spelling, after URL decoding, names a Tenant, and the empty UUID's never does; anything else is refused like a Tenant the Admin holds no role in.

403.description: access_denied, with the problem body, when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a Session restricted to setup, or on a state-changing call a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

put.summary: Change the path Tenant's environment label.
put.description: Tenant Owner only, in an active Tenant. The only request that changes a Tenant's label after creation, and it changes nothing else: no setting or policy changes with it. Removing the Prod label needs a fresh assertion for tenant.label.manage in this Tenant, begun on POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/assertions, which is used up once the locked label is found to be Prod, whatever follows; raising a label, moving between dev and staging, and an unchanged label need none, and any change uses up an unused grant this Session holds for it. A change writes tenancy.tenant.label_changed, or tenancy.tenant.prod_label_removed, on the Tenant's own Log. An unchanged label writes nothing and is 200. A body that isn't JSON, is over 4096 bytes, misses label or has the wrong type, and an unknown label, is 400 tenant_invalid. A Tenant still being created is 409 tenant_not_active.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The Tenant's public ID: ten_ and the UUID's 16 bytes in lowercase RFC 4648 base32 with no padding, whose last character carries two zero bits. Only this canonical spelling, after URL decoding, names a Tenant, and the empty UUID's never does; anything else is refused like a Tenant the Admin holds no role in.

parameters.name: X-Gatekeep-Tenant
parameters.description: The Tenant the page shows, its ten_ ID: it must equal {tenantId}, or 409 tenant_mismatch. It never selects a Tenant.

403.description: fresh_assertion_required, with the problem body, when no fresh assertion for this action and target is bound to the Session; access_denied when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a restricted Session, or a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

409.description: tenant_mismatch, with the problem body, when X-Gatekeep-Tenant is missing, sent twice or isn't {tenantId}, and nothing ran; or another conflict the operation's description names.

get.summary: Search the path Tenant's Log: newest first, 50 a page.
get.description: Any Tenant Role in the path Tenant. Read only, in the Tenant's own scope: no other Tenant's event is ever listed, and the read isn't audited. Each event's evt_ ID, time, type code, the catalogue's outcome and summary, and its Actor and target as internal references; never its detail, so no IP address, User-Agent or email. Every parameter is optional, at most once, and they combine; each filters an indexed envelope column. nextCursor is the last event's ID when an older page follows, else null; pass it back as cursor with the same filters. A parameter sent twice or empty, an unknown outcome, a code that isn't three lower-case parts, a User that is neither a UUID nor an email, an Application that isn't a UUID, a time that isn't an instant, from not before to, or a malformed cursor is 400 invalid_request. An email no event names, like any search that matches nothing, is an empty list. A malformed, unknown or role-less Tenant is 403 access_denied, audited as every Tenant capability refusal is.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The Tenant's public ID: ten_ and the UUID's 16 bytes in lowercase RFC 4648 base32 with no padding, whose last character carries two zero bits. Only this canonical spelling, after URL decoding, names a Tenant, and the empty UUID's never does; anything else is refused like a Tenant the Admin holds no role in.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: One event type code, {domain}.{object}.{action}, as docs/audit-events.md publishes it.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: A User: their UUID, or an email, which resolves first to the User references on this Tenant's events whose detail holds exactly it. Events whose Actor or target is that User.

parameters.name: application
parameters.description: An Application's UUID: events whose Actor or target is that client.

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: success or failure: the events whose type the catalogue gives that outcome.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: An ISO 8601 instant with Z or an offset: events at or after it.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: An ISO 8601 instant with Z or an offset: events before it. It must come after from.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The previous page's nextCursor: an evt_ public ID.

403.description: access_denied, with the problem body, when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a Session restricted to setup, or on a state-changing call a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

get.summary: One event of the path Tenant's Log, with its raw detail for an Editor or Owner.
get.description: Any Tenant Role in the path Tenant. Read only, in the Tenant's own scope, and the read isn't audited. The same fields as a search row. raw is set only when the caller holds tenant.log_detail.read in this Tenant (Editor and Owner): the envelope, the seal (seq, and prevHash and hash in lowercase hex; null while unsealed, prevHash null for a chain's first event) and the detail (IP address, User-Agent and email, each nullable; null when the event has none). For anyone else raw is null and no detail is read. An eventId that isn't an evt_ ID is 400 invalid_request. An event this Tenant doesn't have, including another Tenant's, is 404 not_found. A malformed, unknown or role-less Tenant is 403 access_denied, audited as every Tenant capability refusal is.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The Tenant's public ID: ten_ and the UUID's 16 bytes in lowercase RFC 4648 base32 with no padding, whose last character carries two zero bits. Only this canonical spelling, after URL decoding, names a Tenant, and the empty UUID's never does; anything else is refused like a Tenant the Admin holds no role in.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event's public ID, as the search lists it: evt_ and 26 base32 characters.

403.description: access_denied, with the problem body, when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a Session restricted to setup, or on a state-changing call a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

get.summary: The path Tenant's Signing Keys in every state: next, current, previous, retired and revoked.
get.description: Any Tenant Role in the path Tenant. Its signing keys only, never a Management key: next, then current, then previous, then retired and revoked keys together, newest first; a retired key is listed whether or not its Transit key is destroyed yet. Each key has its key ID (the kid tokens and JWKS carry), its algorithm, its state and when it was created, and nothing of its key material. It reads the database only, so it answers while key custody is down. It writes nothing. A malformed, unknown or role-less Tenant is 403 access_denied, audited as every Tenant capability refusal is.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The Tenant's public ID: ten_ and the UUID's 16 bytes in lowercase RFC 4648 base32 with no padding, whose last character carries two zero bits. Only this canonical spelling, after URL decoding, names a Tenant, and the empty UUID's never does; anything else is refused like a Tenant the Admin holds no role in.

403.description: access_denied, with the problem body, when the capability is refused. No body when an earlier check refuses first: a Session restricted to setup, or on a state-changing call a wrong Origin or CSRF token.

get.summary: The path Tenant's public JWKS sample, as its Tenant host serves it, and the JWKS URI.
get.description: Any Tenant Role in the path Tenant. One public RSA key per published Signing Key (current, then next, then previous), with exactly the members the Tenant's own JWKS serves: kty, use, alg, kid, n and e, never a private member and never a Management key. The public halves come from key custody, and the URI is the Tenant's stored issuer with /.well-known/jwks. Key custody down, or without a published key's version, is 503 for the whole sample. It writes nothing. A malformed, unknown or role-less Tenant is 403 access_denied, audited as every Tenant capability refusal is.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The Tenant's public ID: ten_ and the UUID's 16 bytes in lowercase RFC 4648 base32 with no padding, whose last character carries two zero bits. Only this canonical spelling, after URL decoding, names a Tenant, and the empty UUID's never does; anything else is refused like a Tenant the Admin holds no role in.
